result.subject: Following up: ramp-phase processing skills and a possible training pathway
recipients: Nigerian High Commission Canberra -- Trade Office
result.body:
Thank you for your time today.

To summarise what we discussed. Your Kwinana refinery produced first battery-grade lithium hydroxide in July 2025 and has been ramping toward its 50,000 tpa nameplate since August 2025; the Mt Holland concentrator expansion approved by shareholders in July 2026 doubles spodumene concentrate production and is a separate asset from the refinery. We understood your ramp-phase workforce need to sit in process operations and high-purity quality control.

On our side, the published Australian vocational assessment locates the battery-refining skills gap in exactly those areas -- high-purity quality control, automation, value-chain knowledge and battery chemistry -- rather than in any absence of a training system, with PMA30120 and PMA40116 already mapped to refinery roles. Western Australia lists Metallurgist (ANZSCO 234912) as a state-nominated priority occupation, so the migration instrument exists if a candidate pipeline ever justifies it.

We would like to explore, with no commitment on either side, whether a structured training and placement pathway involving Nigerian-qualified process engineers would be of interest. We should be clear that this is our proposition to test, not an existing arrangement.

I will follow up with a short note on Australian conversion qualifications in extractive metallurgy. Please let me know if a further conversation would be useful.

key_commitments.description: Send a one-page summary of Australian conversion qualifications in extractive metallurgy, with entry requirements.
Confirm whether the mission can convene a Nigerian training counterpart for an exploratory call. No commitment is offered or implied.
